title: Intelligent recap: what Teams generates after a meeting or call, and what controls it
summary: Hold: the page presents meeting memory as enabled for every tenant without Microsoft's Teams TAP preview restriction, and incorrectly attributes all recap storage to the organiser. Audio recap prerequisites and recording-expiration exceptions also need correction; Microsoft documents conflicting guidance about the two newer recap policy parameters.

claims.claim: Intelligent recap provides AI-generated meeting, event and call summaries and notes.
claims.quote: Intelligent recap for Microsoft Teams uses AI technology to improve your users' productivity and efficiency.

claims.claim: Intelligent recap includes AI-recommended tasks.
claims.quote: Your users can access AI-generated notes and recommended tasks for PSTN calls through the **Recap** button in the Calls app in Teams.

claims.claim: Meeting recap includes chapters and topic navigation.
claims.quote: Meeting chapters divide the meeting into chapters, and meeting topics that allow your users to jump to a point in the meeting when a certain topic was discussed.

claims.claim: Users access meeting and event recap through the Recap tab in Teams calendar and chat.
claims.quote: After the meeting or event ends, your users can access the following AI powered features for their meetings through the **Recap** tab in the Teams calendar and chat:

claims.claim: Users access call recap through a Recap button.
claims.quote: Your users can access AI-generated notes and recommended tasks for PSTN calls through the **Recap** button in the Calls app in Teams.

claims.claim: An organisation assigning Copilot or Teams Premium licences and leaving transcription policy on is already producing recaps.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams intelligent recap start transcription meeting automatic AI notes generated transcription policy. Read intelligent-recap-calls-meetings, privacy/intelligent-recap and meeting-transcription-captions; none states that policy alone generates recaps.
claims.fix: Replace the clause beginning 'so an organisation' with 'so an organisation that has assigned Copilot or Teams Premium licences and enabled transcription has made full recap available for transcribed meetings'.

claims.claim: The no-transcript recap can generate a summary when recording and transcription are not enabled.
claims.quote: With this feature, an AI summary is generated even when recording and transcription aren't enabled.

claims.claim: Only the meeting policy parameter AllowIntelligentRecap can switch intelligent recap off for every meeting.
claims.quote: Searched: intelligent recap AllowIntelligentRecap Teams admin center toggle turn off meetings calls; intelligent recap AI summary delete administrator policy disable without saving transcripts. Read no-transcript recap and Copilot policy pages; neither establishes exclusivity in those terms.
claims.fix: Remove 'Only' and replace the sentence with 'The meeting policy parameter -AllowIntelligentRecap switches intelligent recap off for all meetings under that policy, whether or not transcripts are saved.' Keep the source disagreement qualification specified for controls[0].api.

claims.claim: Turning intelligent recap off makes the related settings unavailable in Teams.
claims.quote: Turning off intelligent recap disables intelligent recap for all meetings, regardless of whether transcripts are saved, and the related settings are unavailable in Teams.

claims.claim: Intelligent recap needs a Microsoft 365 subscription including Teams, or a no-Teams subscription plus a separate Teams licence.
claims.quote: You must assign your users a Microsoft 365 subscription that includes Teams or a Microsoft 365 (no Teams) subscription with a separate Teams license.

claims.claim: Intelligent text recap requires Teams Premium or Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote: Intelligent text recap requires a Teams Premium or Microsoft Copilot license.

claims.quote: For Public Switched Telephone Network (PSTN) calls, you must also assign a Teams Phone license and have a calling plan for your users.

claims.claim: The recap pages publish licence requirements but no separate recap meter, per-use charge or price.
claims.quote: Searched: "intelligent recap" "pricing" "meter". Read intelligent-recap-calls-meetings, intelligent-recap-without-saving-transcripts and manage-meeting-recaps-app in full; their licensing sections name licences, not a separate recap meter or price.

claims.claim: Storage for recap files falls on the organiser's OneDrive, SharePoint or Exchange.
claims.quote: AI-generated notes are stored in an Exchange folder in the mailboxes of the meeting participants.
claims.fix: Replace 'Storage for recap files falls on the organiser's OneDrive, SharePoint or Exchange' with 'The no-transcript Word summary is stored in the organiser's OneDrive; meeting notes and tasks are stored in participants' Exchange mailboxes, while chapters and topics are stored with the recording in OneDrive or SharePoint'.

claims.claim: The Microsoft recap pages read give no recap-specific storage charge.
claims.quote: Searched: "intelligent recap" "storage" "charge"; intelligent recap storage costs charges pricing per use OneDrive Exchange Teams Premium Microsoft 365 Copilot license. Read recap overview, no-transcript recap and privacy pages; no recap-specific storage rate was stated.

claims.claim: Prices sit on the Teams Premium and Microsoft 365 Copilot licensing pages.

claims.fix: Remove 'Prices sit on the Teams Premium and Microsoft 365 Copilot licensing pages'.

claims.claim: No admin centre toggle for AllowIntelligentRecap was found at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: "AllowIntelligentRecap" "admin center"; intelligent recap AllowIntelligentRecap Teams admin center toggle turn off meetings calls. Read no-transcript recap, Teams Premium overview and Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy; no admin centre path for this parameter was documented.

claims.where: controls[0].api; controls[0].note; Why it matters; Risks and limits
claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policyname> -AllowIntelligentRecap $false disables recap for all meetings under the policy.
claims.quote: To turn off intelligent recap, use the [Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy](/en-us/powershell/module/microsoftteams/set-csteamsmeetingpolicy) cmdlet and set the `-AllowIntelligentRecap` parameter to `$false`.
claims.fix: Keep the command, but add to the row note and the existing documentation-conflict paragraph: 'The no-transcript recap page documents this switch as effective, while the Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy reference says under -AllowIntelligentRecap: "This feature has not been fully released yet, so the setting will have no effect." Microsoft has not reconciled these statements.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoftteams/set-csteamsmeetingpolicy.

claims.claim: Meeting transcription is configured in Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Transcription.
claims.quote:
In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to **Meetings** > **Meeting policies**.
2. Select the policy that you want to edit or create a new one.
3. Toggle **Transcription** **On** or **Off**.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowTranscription $true allows meeting transcription.
claims.quote:
### -AllowTranscription

Determines whether post-meeting captions and transcriptions are allowed in a user's meetings. Set this to TRUE to allow. Set this to FALSE to prohibit.

claims.claim: Both the organiser's transcription policy and the policy of the person starting transcription matter.
claims.quote: Transcription is both a per-organizer and per-user policy setting. For meetings and events to include transcripts, the organizer must have this setting turned on. The user who starts the recording or transcript must also have this setting turned on.

claims.claim: Meeting transcription is On by default for new policies.
claims.quote: Toggle **Transcription** **On** or **Off**. This setting is **On** by default for new policies.

claims.claim: Call transcription is configured in Teams admin center > Voice > Calling policies > policy > Transcription.
claims.quote:
In the Microsoft Teams admin center, select **Voice** > **Calling policies**.
2. Select the policy you want to modify.
3. Turn **Transcription** to **On**.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowTranscriptionForCalling $true enables call transcription.
claims.quote:
For example, this script enables transcription for the global policy:

```powershell
Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy -Identity Global -AllowTranscriptionForCalling $true
```

claims.claim: Call transcription is off by default.
claims.quote: Transcription is automatically generated, recorded text of what was said in a call. When turned on, the transcript is available to users to review after a call ends. This setting is off by default.

claims.claim: The Copilot setting is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Recording & transcription > Copilot.
claims.quote:
In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to **Meetings** > **Meeting policies**.
2. Select an existing policy or create a new one.
3. Go to the **Recording & transcription** section and find the **Copilot** setting.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -Copilot Disabled sets the organiser's default Copilot option to Off.
claims.quote:
To set the organizer's default Copilot option to **Off** and allow them to change it, use the following script:

```PowerShell
Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -Copilot Disabled
```

claims.claim: The other Copilot parameter values include Enabled, EnabledWithTranscript and EnabledWithTranscriptDefaultOn.
claims.quote: | On | Enabled | ... | On with saved transcript required | EnabledWithTranscript | ... | On with transcript saved by default | EnabledWithTranscriptDefaultOn |

claims.claim: Organisers can change the Copilot option per meeting depending on their assigned policy value.
claims.quote: Organizers can change this value to **During and after the meeting**, and **Off**.

claims.claim: The no-transcript docx expiry setting is under Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Copilot and other AI.
claims.quote: Under **Copilot and other AI**, next to **Set a default expiration time for Intelligent Recap .docx files for non-transcribed meetings**, enter the number of days that documents are retained.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policyname> -IntelligentRecapDocxFileExpirationDays <days> sets recap document expiry.
claims.quote: Use the [Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy](/en-us/powershell/module/microsoftteams/set-csteamsmeetingpolicy) cmdlet with the `-IntelligentRecapDocxFileExpirationDays` parameter.
claims.fix: Keep the command, but add to the note: 'The no-transcript recap page documents this parameter as effective; the Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy reference says under -IntelligentRecapDocxFileExpirationDays: "This feature has not been fully released yet, so the setting will have no effect." Microsoft has not reconciled the pages.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoftteams/set-csteamsmeetingpolicy.

claims.claim: The recap docx expiry period accepts 1 to 9999 days, or -1 for no expiration.
claims.quote: You can specify a value from **1** to **9999** days, or **-1** for no expiration.

claims.claim: The recording and transcript automatic-expiry control is under Meetings > Meeting policies > Recording & transcription.
claims.quote: After turning on **Recordings and transcriptions automatically expire**, you'll get the option to set the **Default expiration time**, measured in days.
claims.fix: Use 'Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Recording & transcription > Recordings and transcriptions automatically expire' for the existing toggle. Add to the row note: 'When automatic expiry is on, set Default expiration time to choose the number of days.' The current route omits selection of the policy and stops before the duration setting.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -NewMeetingRecordingExpirationDays <days> sets recording expiration time.
claims.quote:
To set the expiration time using PowerShell, run the following command:

```powershell
Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -NewMeetingRecordingExpirationDays <days>
```

claims.claim: Meeting policies can be assigned to users or groups.
claims.quote: You can apply your Copilot meeting policies to groups or individual users.

claims.claim: There is no separate policy setting for no-transcript recap; disabling intelligent recap under the policy also disables that variant.
claims.quote: There isn't a separate policy setting for intelligent recap without saving transcripts. To prevent users from using this feature while keeping Copilot enabled, turn off intelligent recap in the Teams meeting policy.

claims.claim: Meeting organisers can delete the no-transcript AI summary from the Recap tab.
claims.quote: Meeting organizers can delete the AI summary from the **Recap** tab or the corresponding Word document in OneDrive.

claims.claim: No admin switch governing organiser deletion of the no-transcript AI summary is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: intelligent recap AI summary delete administrator policy disable without saving transcripts. Read no-transcript recap FAQ, policy controls and cmdlet reference. No administrator switch governing organiser deletion of that Word summary was found.

claims.claim: The Teams Premium overview says admins cannot turn intelligent meeting recap on or off, whereas the no-transcript page documents a policy cmdlet.
claims.quote: | Intelligent meeting recap | No, contact support for assistance.^1^ |

claims.claim: The read Microsoft documentation does not establish whether AllowIntelligentRecap also disables call recap.
claims.quote: Searched: intelligent recap AllowIntelligentRecap Teams admin center toggle turn off meetings calls. Read no-transcript recap, call recap prerequisites, Teams Premium calls section and Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy's AllowIntelligentRecap entry; its documented scope is meetings, not calls.

claims.quote: Microsoft 365 OneDrive Storage is a pay-as-you-go service that allows organizations to extend OneDrive storage beyond licensed limits and pay only for storage consumed above their included quota.
